chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad from Mu'alla ibn Muhammad from Al-Hasan ibn Ali al-Washsha from Abdullah ibn Sinan from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said:
Rasool-Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'The habitual drinker of wine will meet Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, on the Day he meets Him, as an infidel.'

key_terms.مُدْمِنُ: The habitual one / one who is addicted to

ai.seo_question: What is the spiritual state of a habitual wine drinker on the Day of Judgment according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In al-Kafi, Shaykh al-Kulayni records this chain to highlight the jurisprudential distinction between occasional and habitual consumption, where the latter leads to a state of 'kufr' (disbelief) not necessarily of apostasy but of spiritual alienation. This reflects the Shia scholarly view that persistent neglect of a known prohibition erodes the foundation of faith, a concept often discussed in commentaries on the verse of abrogation regarding wine. The hadith serves as a stern warning that chronic indulgence transforms a sin into a defining characteristic of the believer's spiritual state.
